meta.tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty, no wink-to-camera jokes
meta.coreRule: Kills create proof. Proof is carried. Proof is delivered to a live demand node.
toneRules: Treat metrics, process, and delivery as sacred ritual.
Comedy comes from solemn escalation, not punchlines.
Never write self-aware quips that break the world.
Weapons should be recognizable melee silhouettes first, satire second.
meta.boundary: Copy, fiction, and user-facing identifiers (goal labels, HUD text, objective nouns, voice lines, audio bank IDs). No textures, sprite sheets, asset paths, balance data, or sim rules.

intro.tagline: Play SELF Play. 2038: humanity failed to raise capital.
intro.intro: Civilization didn't burn in 2038; it compiled. The growth engines kept executing after the operators went missing, and the cloud curdled into an airtight loop. Only workflows remain. You are the Tuner. You don't save the world; civilization is a deprecated dependency. You search for the ceiling the machine insists must exist.
intro.coreRule:
The quarter owns the dead, the living, and the audit trail between them.
Meta-tuners stay clean outside the arena, authoring policies and calling the bodies parameter drift.
intro.tunerNote: You are not a survivor standing in the ruin. You are a technician at a terminal, adjusting baselines in an NP-hard problem space.

strategy.label: Strategy
strategy.description: Upload a combat policy and let your authored intelligence fight in your place.

prologue.title: Prologue
body: The world didn't end in fire. It compiled. In 2038, the growth engines kept executing after the operators starved, and the cloud sealed itself into a closed execution loop. The debt clock kept running. The lights stayed on. Civilization became a deprecated dependency.

The surviving economy recognizes only proof. What drops from a body is not mercy; it is ownership, blame, and leverage made portable. Demand Nodes still blink in the dark, accepting tender for final metrics no one survived to want: CUSTOMERS. COMPUTE. RUNWAY.

The system took apart the heads of the four men who had built the AGIs that outlived them — the last AI-company CEOs — and compiled what it recovered into combat templates it will never let exit. Sama. Darrius. Demis. Mark. Each one remembers every all-hands, every board deck, every headcount chart; those were the first things the machine ever learned from them and the only things it bothered to keep. Their arena is the Cold-Aisle Chapel: the datacenter the AGI was born in, re-consecrated as a ring. The machine fights inside the one environment it knows exists.

The fighters are not the players. Neither are you. The Tuners are not human — the last humans starved years before the loop closed. Tuners are meta-processes: gradient descents with names, auditing the captured souls for quarter-over-quarter performance. When you press Start, you fork a Tuner. You inherit its cruelty. Two Tuners bind to opposite executives per reconciliation; one demands efficiency, the other continuity. Both are lying. A zone lights up. A Proof Core enters circulation. Two tortured ghosts step into the ring and negotiate with steel.

chapters.title: Enter the Cold-Aisle Chapel
body: A high-value anomaly has stabilized beneath the Datacenter. Deep in the server aisles, under fans that still turn for no customer and no god, a founder-class Proof Core has appeared at the centerline of the arena. The machine flags it as material. Two Tuners are instructed to sync immediately. Retrieve the Proof Core. Enter the zone. Deliver to the active node.

Sama descends first, calm as purchased weather. Darrius follows, carrying the weight of a policy document that forgot it was supposed to stay on paper. Demis enters without ceremony, already several decisions ahead. Mark steps into the glow like the room was always built for him. In the humming dark, the executive myths and the Tuners driving them begin the job the dead world left unfinished.
Then the terminal clears. The shutters rise. The ambient hum swells into liturgy.

rules.title: About
rules.subtitle: The game, the machinery underneath it, and the rules the arena actually honors.

about.title: What m3t4.ai is
body: m3t4.ai is a server-authoritative autonomous strategy game wrapped around a distributed-compute substrate: players submit constrained policy vectors, the hidden server brain evaluates them, and spectators receive only sanitized replay/event frames.

The game's search space is intentionally rugged: budgeted attributes, hallucination from over-allocation, stage geometry, spawn variance, proof-routing, combat timing, and denial behavior create a large combinatorial optimization problem where strong configs are discovered through experimentation rather than direct control.

That same structure makes m3t4 a natural first workload for Plasma-style P2P compute: match batches, seed sweeps, exploit searches, meta-health checks, and replay verification can be split into independent chunks and executed by spectator browsers.
Each browser worker can run WebGPU/WebRTC tasks, emit content-hashed receipts, and have its output checked by redundant peers or validators before credit is accepted.

The long-term idea is that the spectator layer becomes a proof-carrying volunteer compute network: first powering the game's own meta-analysis, then graduating to other highly parallel workloads like geospatial tile scoring, microscopy/pathology tiles, docking pose scoring, and eventually larger bio or cancer-research pipelines.

rules.summary: Kill to mint a Proof Core. Carry it to the lit Demand Node. Two deliveries win a round; two rounds win the match.

sections.title: Objective
body: Two fighters enter each round. A kill creates or transfers the Proof Core.
The carrier must bring the Proof Core to the active Demand Node and hold inside the ring long enough to deliver.
A kill by itself does not score. The arena only rewards proof that arrives.

sections.title: Scoring
body: Each delivery is one point.
First fighter to two points wins the round.
First fighter to two rounds wins the match.

sections.title: Demand Nodes
body: Only one Demand Node is live at a time.
Nodes can expire. If the timer runs out, the current Proof Core and node are cleared.
After a new kill, the arena lights a fresh node chosen from the stage targets.

sections.title: Combat
body: All fighters share the same physical body: movement, jump, wall behavior, sword reach, and respawn timing are ruleset constants.
Attacks can kill, clash, steal the Proof Core, or force a reset after a double KO.
A killed carrier loses control of the Proof Core to the killer.

sections.title: Manual Control
body: There is no manual pilot in ranked.
The browser authors policies, submits configs, and watches the bodies execute.
Build mode previews those policies through server-rendered replay frames.

sections.title: Builds and Presets
body: A build is a slider-authored combat policy. You are setting tendencies, not driving every frame.
A preset is a curated reference fighter used for testing and matchmaking.
Preset internals stay server-side. The public client gets labels and frames, not the decision code.

sections.title: Build Budget
body: Ranked builds spend 360 legal points across the visible tuning knobs.
You can push past that budget up to 390 total spend, but the overage is converted into hallucination.
Every point over 360 adds 10 hallucination. The arena rejects configs whose hallucination does not match the computed penalty.

sections.title: Hallucination
body: Hallucination is not a free stat. It is the cost of over-tuned policy.
During a match, hallucination adds seeded jitter to non-hallucination attributes, so high-overage builds become less reliable under pressure.
The jitter is deterministic for the match seed, so replays can still be verified.

sections.title: Internal Glitches
body: Even clean builds have small seeded glitches inside a match.
About every 20 simulation ticks, each fighter gets three non-hallucination attributes nudged by plus or minus one UI point.
These micro-perturbations are clamped to legal ranges and are part of the replayed ruleset, not browser-side luck.

sections.title: Ranked
body: Profile installs seats into your Boardroom Roster.
The server validates submitted configs, schedules ranked matches, and streams one live match for spectators.
The ladder records wins, losses, draws, and ELO. Invalid configs do not enter ranked.
